claims.text: Adding 1 wt% Ce to boride-based components improves their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
The Ce-modified components will exhibit a 35% improvement in corrosion resistance relative to unmodified boride-based components.
The proposed improvement will remain effective between 600°C and 700°C in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
Adding Ce causes formation of a protective, Ce-enriched oxide layer on the component surface.
Ce reacts with oxygen to form an oxide layer under the proposed service conditions.
The resulting Ce-containing oxide layer is stable and dense.
The oxide layer acts as a barrier against penetration by molten aluminum.
Suppressing molten-aluminum penetration reduces subsequent corrosion of the boride-based component.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on processing conditions, the type of boride-based component, and impurities or other elements.
The hypothesis is to be tested by comparing corrosion rate and surface morphology of Ce-modified and unmodified components in a controlled corrosion test.
The hypothesis is falsified if the modified components do not show at least a 25% lower corrosion rate than the unmodified controls.

contradictions.description: The point prediction is a 35% improvement, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis below 25% improvement. Thus, results from 25% up to less than 35% would contradict the stated quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
